bib.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners

question: Does finetuning a language model on a collection of tasks phrased as natural-language instructions improve its zero-shot performance on unseen task types?
hypothesis: Instruction tuning on a diverse set of tasks improves performance on unseen tasks.
contributions: Instruction tuning: finetune a 137B pretrained LM on 62 NLP datasets verbalized via instruction templates (FLAN)
Evaluation on held-out task clusters so no dataset of the same task type is seen in tuning
Ablations on number of clusters, model scale, role of instructions, few-shot exemplars and prompt tuning

method.summary: LaMDA-PT 137B is finetuned on a mixture of 62 TFDS text datasets in 12 task clusters, each rendered with 10 hand-written instruction templates. To test unseen tasks, one model is tuned per held-out cluster with that cluster (and related clusters) removed, then evaluated zero-shot against LaMDA-PT, GPT-3 175B and GLaM.

datasets.name: Instruction tuning mixture (62 TFDS datasets, 12 clusters)
datasets.size: 62 datasets; at most 30k examples per dataset; examples-proportional mixing with rate maximum 3k
datasets.split: training splits; each held-out cluster (and related clusters) removed per model
datasets.source: publicly available datasets on Tensorflow Datasets; 10 manually written templates per dataset (up to 3 turn-the-task-around)
datasets.preprocessing: Examples formatted with a randomly selected template per dataset; OPTIONS suffix for classification; packing of examples into one sequence with EOS between input and target

datasets.name: 25 NLU/NLG evaluation datasets across NLI, reading comp., closed-book QA, translation, commonsense, coreference, struct-to-text (Tables 1-2)
datasets.size: not summarised; e.g. ANLI R1 1,000 and PIQA 1,838 test examples
datasets.split: test sets; dev set used to pick best template
datasets.preprocessing: Summarization not evaluated because mean input exceeds 1024 tokens

datasets.name: SuperGLUE (prompt tuning analysis)
datasets.size: full train set or 32 training examples

models.name: LaMDA-PT 137B
models.init_from: pretrained on web documents (incl. code), dialog data, Wikipedia; 2.49T BPE tokens
models.context: inferred: 1024 input + 256 target tokens in finetuning

other.pretraining_energy: 451 MWh, 26 tCO2e (same models as Austin et al. 2021)

other.checkpoints: one model per held-out task cluster

other.note: text says 422M, Fig 7 axis label says 0.4B
numbers taken from Brown et al. 2020
numbers taken from Du et al. 2021

training.objective: inferred: next-token (supervised) loss on targets of instruction-formatted examples
training.compute: fewer than 2% of the pretraining gradient steps

other.checkpoint: final checkpoint at 30k steps for all evaluations
other.prompt_tuning: Lester et al. 2021 procedure with prompt length 10, weight decay 1e-4, no dropout on attention scores
other.few_shot_flan: exemplars randomly drawn from train set at training and inference time; capped at 16 and total length under 960 tokens

inference.decoding: greedy search for generative tasks (Brown et al. used beam search)
inference.samples: mean and std over up to 10 templates per dataset (#t in Tables 1-2); one best-dev-template run; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot natural-language instruction template plus OPTIONS suffix; few-shot FLAN concatenates instruct(x_i)+y_i; LaMDA-PT baseline uses GPT-3 prompts with the highest k in {1,3,5,10} fitting 1024 tokens

parameters.curly_brackets: DROP and SQuADv2 answers delimited by { }

metrics.name: accuracy / exact match / F1 / BLEU / ROUGE
metrics.definition: accuracy or EM by default; F1 for DROP, MultiRC, SQuAD v1/v2; BLEU for translation; ROUGE for struct-to-text

eval.protocol: Unseen task = no dataset from any cluster D belongs to seen in tuning; one model per held-out cluster; report mean over templates and test score of best-dev template; data contamination check with ~13-gram overlap following Brown et al. 2020; no significance test, single tuning run stated

availability.data: datasets public via Tensorflow Datasets; templates in Appendix G

results.claim: Average held-out accuracy rises from 49.9 to 63.5 as instruction tuning clusters go from 1 to 7.
results.setup: Held-out NLI, commonsense, closed-book QA; clusters added in decreasing size order; 137B
results.quote: As expected, we observe that average performance across the three held-out clusters improves as we add additional clusters
results.note: Performance does not saturate at 7 clusters; sentiment cluster adds minimal value.

results.claim: Instruction tuning hurts held-out performance for models of 8B and smaller, helps at 68B and 137B.
results.setup: Same split as 4.1 (13 held-out tasks avg); sizes 422M, 2B, 8B, 68B, 137B
results.quote: instruction tuning actually hurts performance on held-out tasks
results.note: Authors' explanation (capacity filled by ~40 tuning tasks) is a hypothesis, not tested.

results.claim: Tuning with natural instructions gives 55.2 four-cluster average vs 37.3 with no template, 46.6 and 47.0 with dataset-name prompts.
results.setup: Zero-shot, four held-out clusters (NLI, read. comp., closed-book QA, translation)
results.table: Table 3, rows Natural instructions (= FLAN), No template, Task/dataset name; column Four-Task Average (55.2, 37.3, 46.6, 47.0)
results.note: Dataset-name NLI score is inflated by CB 83.9 on a 56-example validation set.

results.claim: More datasets per cluster improved held-out performance by almost 10%; more templates had negligible effect.
results.setup: 1 vs 4 datasets per cluster, 1/4/10 templates per dataset; held-out NLI, commonsense, closed-book QA
results.quote: Using more datasets per cluster improved performance by almost 10% on average across the three held-out clusters.

results.setup: SuperGLUE dev average; 32 train examples: 63.8 (LaMDA-PT) vs 78.1 (FLAN); full train set: 79.1 vs 87.4
results.note: Figure 10 label order is read from text positions; averages of Table 4 rows reproduce 63.8 and 78.1.

limits: Subjectivity in assigning tasks to clusters
Only short, typically one-sentence instructions explored
Individual evaluation examples may appear in pretraining data; post-hoc analysis found no evidence of substantial effect
Single cluster split for scaling ablation (authors say cross-validation would be better)
Context 1024 tokens so summarization not evaluated; mostly English
Not useful for tasks formatted as language modeling (commonsense, coreference)
Zero-shot DROP and SQuADv2 GPT-3 numbers use same-passage exemplars, not comparable
Simple failures: returning the nth word, translating a question instead of answering

terms.definition: finetuning language models on a collection of datasets described via instructions
dataset D is unseen only if no dataset from any task cluster D belongs to was seen during instruction tuning
token OPTIONS appended to classification tasks along with the list of output classes
